rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zajjaj prefers أنما إلهكم with fatḥa; إنما with kasra is also grammatically possible because يوحى إلي means that revelation is spoken to the Prophet, though the reading has fatḥa.
rows.anchor: ولكن القراءة الفتح لا غير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: آذنتكم means I informed you of what is revealed to me so that you may be equal in believing it.
rows.anchor: أعلمتكم بما يوحى إلي لتستووا في الإيمان به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet does not know whether what he has announced will be a trial for the audience; فتنة here means a test.
rows.anchor: أي وما أدري ما آذنتكم به فتنة لكم أي اختبار لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The segment records قل رب احكم بالحق and قال ربي أحكم بالحق as read alternatives to قال رب احكم بالحق.
rows.anchor: ويقرأ: (قل رب احكم بالحق).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command احكم means judge, as in the earlier messengers’ prayer; God directed the Prophet to say رب احكم بالحق.
rows.anchor: وكان من مضى من الرسل يقولون: (ربنا افتح بيننا وبين قومنا بالحق).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Lord is the one whose aid is sought against what the audience says falsely.
rows.anchor: (وربنا الرحمن المستعان على ما تصفون). أي على ما تكذبون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading منسكا points here to sacrifice, supported by the command to invoke God over livestock He provided.
rows.anchor: المنسك في هذا الموضع يدل على معنى النحر

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some take المنسك to mean a place that must be tended; Zajjaj says this interpretation is permissible.
rows.anchor: المنسك الموضع الذي يجب تعهده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the form منسك, the word means a place of ritual, by analogy with مخلس as a place of slipping.
rows.anchor: ومن قال منسك فمعناه مكان نسك مثل مخلس مكان خلوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form منسك can instead function as a verbal noun, like النسك and النّسوك.
rows.anchor: ومن قال منسك فهو بمعنى المصدر نحو النسك والنسوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ritual enables each community to invoke God’s name over the livestock He has provided, that is, over its slaughter.
rows.anchor: المعنى ليذكروا اسم الله على نحر ما رزقهم من بهيمة الأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God is one, no one but Him should be named over sacrificial animals.
rows.anchor: أي لا ينبغي أن تذكروا على ذبائحكم إلا الله وحده

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation calls the المخبتون humble people.
rows.anchor: قيل المخبتون المتواضعون

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation calls the المخبتون those secure in faith in God.
rows.anchor: وقيل المخبتون المطمئنون بالإيمان بالله عز وجل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further explanation describes them as people who do not wrong others and do not retaliate when wronged; Zajjaj accepts all these senses.
rows.anchor: الذين لا يظلمون وإذا ظلموا لم ينتصروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مخبت derives from خبت, a low part of the land, so every مخبت is humble.
rows.anchor: اشتقاقه من الخبت من الأرض وهي المكان المنخفض منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transmitted reading has genitive والمقيمي الصلاة without nun, parsed as an iḍāfa construction.
rows.anchor: إسقاط التنوين، والخفض على الإضافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: المقيمين الصلاة is also grammatically possible, although it differs from the written codex.
rows.anchor: الصلاة، إلا أنه بخلاف المصحف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A more remote parsing drops the nun and makes الصلاة accusative because the phrase is long; Sibawayh cites الحافظو as an example and calls the construction anomalous.
rows.anchor: على حذف النون ونصب الصلاة لطول الاسم، وأنشد سيبويه: الحافظو عورة العشيرة لا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accusative البدن is better because a verb precedes it; an implied جعلنا governs it, explained by the verb already stated.
rows.anchor: النصب أحسن لأن قبله فعلا، المعنى وجعلنا البدن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raising البدن is also possible if it begins a new sentence.
rows.anchor: وإن شئت رفعت على الاستئناف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: البدن is pronounced with dāl either quiescent or with ḍamma; بدنة/بدن and بدن follow the singular/plural patterns of ثمرة/ثمر/ثمر.
rows.anchor: بدنة وبدن، وبدن مثل قوله ثمرة وثمر وثمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sacrificial camel is called بدنة because it becomes fat.
rows.anchor: بدنة لأنها تبدن، أي تسمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: صواف is an accusative circumstantial expression and has no tanwin because it is diptote.
rows.anchor: منصوبة على الحال، ولكنها لا تنون لأنها لا تنصرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: صواف means the camels’ legs are aligned; the name of God is recited over them while they are being slaughtered.
rows.anchor: فاذكروا اسم الله عليها في حال نحرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Camels are slaughtered standing, and the verse indicates this practice.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية تدل على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading صوافن describes a camel standing on three legs with one foreleg tied when it is to be slaughtered.
rows.anchor: والصافن الذي يقوم على ثلاث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading صوافي, with yāʾ and fatḥa but no tanwin, means camels dedicated solely to God; no other is associated with the invocation at slaughter.
rows.anchor: أي خالصة لله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وجبت جنوبها means that the animals’ sides have fallen to the ground.
rows.anchor: أي إذا سقطت إلى الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source gives the rāʾ as doubled in القانع والمعتر and also allows the form المعتري with a long vowel.
rows.anchor: بتشديد الراء، ويجوز والمعتري بالماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb وجب can mean a wall falling, a heart moving from fear, or a sale becoming binding; each is conjugated with the imperfect يجب.
rows.anchor: المستقبل في ذلك كله يجب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: القانع is explained as someone content with what is given, or someone content with little.
rows.anchor: في القانع الذي يقنع بما تعطيه

rows.speaker: أهل اللغة
rows.claim: The lexicographers’ view is that القانع is a beggar; al-Shammākh’s verse uses القنوع to mean asking.
rows.anchor: وهو مذهب أهل اللغة السائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قنع قناعة means to be satisfied, so قنع is a person who is content, in contrast to the beggar قانع.
rows.anchor: وقنع قناعة إذا رضي فهو قنع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: المعتر is someone who comes to you and asks for what you have; المعتري has the same sense.
rows.anchor: الذي يعتريك فيطلب ما عندك، سألك إذ سئلت عن السؤال

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says the threatened slanderers are those who accuse the Prophet’s wives.
rows.anchor: يعنى به أزواج النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the passage began with the affair of Aisha and then came to cover anyone who slanders believing women.
rows.anchor: الأصل فيه أمر عائشة، ثم صار لكل من رمى المؤمنات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning believing women suffices because accusing a woman entails accusing a believing man; similarly, clothing said to protect from heat also protects from cold, as in 16:81.
rows.anchor: فاستغنى عن ذكر المؤمنين لأنه قد جرى ذكر المؤمنين والمؤمنات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the reading الحق, al-Ḥaqq describes God, so God as the True one gives them their due religion or recompense.
rows.anchor: فالحق من صفة الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the reading دينهم الحق, الحق describes their recompense, and دين means the recompense that is due.
rows.anchor: الحق من صفة الذين والدين ههنا الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation takes the khabīthāt and ṭayyibāt as foul and good utterances: foul men and women speak foul words, and the pure speak good words.
rows.anchor: المعنى الكلمات الخبيثات للخبيثين من الرجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation takes the words as accusations that attach to vile men and women, while nothing attaches to pure women.
rows.anchor: إنما تلصق بالخبيثين من الرجال والخبيثات من النساء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation pairs vile women with vile men and pure women with pure men.
rows.anchor: الخبيثات من النساء للخبيثين من الرجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading تشقق with a doubled shīn means تتشقق, the sky splits apart.
rows.anchor: ويقرأ (تشقق) بتشديد الشين والمعنى تتشقق

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: The reported interpretation has each heaven split in turn and the angels descend to earth, linked to 89:22.
rows.anchor: وتنزل الملائكة إلى الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الحق is an adjective describing الملك: real kingship on Judgment Day belongs to the Merciful.
rows.anchor: ومعناه أن الملك الذي هو الملك حقا هو ملك الرحمن يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transient kingship of this world is as if it were not kingship; the verse echoes the question in 40:16.
rows.anchor: لأن الملك الزائل كأنه ليس بملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accusative الحق is grammatically possible but has not been read, so Zajjaj says not to recite it.
rows.anchor: ولم يقرأ بها فلا تقرأن بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If الحق were accusative, it could be an emphatic assertion of the truth or an explanatory apposition meaning I mean the truth.
rows.anchor: ويكون النصب على وجهين: أحدهما على معنى الملك يومئذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report identifies the wrongdoer as Uqba ibn Abi Muʿayṭ: after Umayya ibn Khalaf threatened to disown him if he converted, Uqba refrained and later regrets it, wishing he had followed the Prophet toward Paradise.
rows.anchor: وأنه كان عزم على الإسلام فبلغ ذلك أمية بن خلف

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some say فلانا خليلا means Satan; the verse about Satan abandoning the human supports this reading, and Zajjaj allows that accepting Umayya’s pressure could also be Satan’s work.
rows.anchor: أي لم أتخذ الشيطان خليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: اتخذت may be pronounced with the ذال distinct or assimilated into tāʾ; assimilation is more frequent and better.
rows.anchor: وبإدغامها في التاء، والإدغام أكثر وأجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their question أهذا الذي بعث الله رسولا means they say, Is this the one God sent to us as a messenger?
rows.anchor: يقولون: أهذا الذي بعث الله إلينا رسولا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One report says a pagan worshipped a stone, then abandoned it for a better-looking stone he passed and worshipped that instead.
rows.anchor: فإذا مر بحجر أحسن منه ترك الأول وعبد الثاني

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation says they make desire their god by obeying and following it without caring about the consequences.
rows.anchor: أي أطاع هواه وركبه فلم يبال عاقبة ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وكيلا means a guardian or custodian.
rows.anchor: أي حفيظا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They resemble cattle in lacking discernment about the signs and proofs presented to them.
rows.anchor: معناه ما هم إلا كالأنعام في قلة التمييز فيما جعل دليلا لهم من الآيات والبرهان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are even more astray because cattle praise and prostrate to God, while these people’s hearts are as hard as stones or harder, as in 2:74.
rows.anchor: تسبح بحمد الله وتسجد له وهم كما قال الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is read both تأمرنا, you command us, and يأمرنا, he commands us.
rows.anchor: وتقرأ (يأمرنا) (1)، والرحمن اسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Raḥmān is a divine name found in earlier scriptures, though the audience did not know it as one of God’s names; they were told it was, as in 17:110.
rows.anchor: والرحمن اسم من أسماء الله مذكور في الكتب الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic usage al-Raḥmān means the possessor of mercy beyond which there is no greater mercy; faʿlān is an intensive pattern for the utmost degree.
rows.anchor: ذو الرحمة التي لا غاية بعدها في الرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pattern’s intensity is illustrated by عطشان, ريان, فرحان, جذلان, and خزيان for the extremes of thirst, satiety, joy, and disgrace.
rows.anchor: رجل عطشان وريان إذا كان في النهاية في الري والعطش

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation identifies the بروج as the large stars.
rows.anchor: البروج: قيل هي الكواكب العظام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A برج is a gap between the eyebrows, and anything conspicuous and elevated is also described as برج; the heavenly برج are so named for their visibility, separation, and height.
rows.anchor: كل ظاهر مرتفع فقد برج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is read سراجا or سرجا; the latter is also allowed with a quiescent rāʾ.
rows.anchor: بتسكين الراء مثل رسل ورسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With سراجا, the lamp is the sun, as in 71:16; with سرجا, it means the sun together with the large stars.
rows.anchor: فمن قرأ سراجا عنى الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: رسول رب العالمين means the message of the Lord of the Worlds, that is, bearers of His message; the quoted poem uses برسول in this sense.
rows.anchor: أي ذوو رسالة رب العالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أن is in the accusative position: the request is that Pharaoh send the Children of Israel along with them.
rows.anchor: موضع (أن) نصب، المعنى أرسلنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وليدا means a newborn at the time of birth.
rows.anchor: أي مولودا حين ولدت

rows.speaker: سيبويه والخليل وجميع البصريين
rows.claim: The lifespan word عمر has three vocalizations in ordinary use; in an oath only the open-vowel form لعمر الله is allowed, according to Sibawayh, al-Khalil, and the Basrans.
rows.anchor: فأما في القسم فلا يجوز إلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh reproaches Moses for having been raised in his household from birth until he grew up.
rows.anchor: فاعتد فرعون على موسى بأنه رباه وليدا منذ ولد إلى أن كبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fatḥa reading فعلتك is better and more common, treating the killing as a single occurrence; al-Shaʿbi’s kasra reading فعلتك describes the manner of the act, illustrated by the distinction between a sitting once and a way of sitting.
rows.anchor: على مذهب المرة الواحدة، وقرأ الشعبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وأنت من الكافرين may mean that Moses was ungrateful for Pharaoh’s favor, or that he was a disbeliever by committing the killing.
rows.anchor: أحدهما من الكافرين لنعمتي، والآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses denies being an unbeliever and admits that he committed the deed in ignorance; a reading substitutes الجاهلين for الضالين.
rows.anchor: واعترف بأن فعله ذلك جهل فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is also read وأنا من الجاهلين.
rows.anchor: أي من الجاهلين، وقد قرئت: وأنا من الجاهلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The حكم God gave Moses means the Torah, which contains God’s legal judgments.
rows.anchor: يعنى التوراة التي فيها حكم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentators read Pharaoh’s words as a reproach, not an acknowledgment of a real favor: how could enslaving the Israelites be a blessing to Moses?
rows.anchor: جهة الإنكار أن تكون تلك نعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although phrased as a statement, the wording rebukes Pharaoh; it implies Moses said the enslavement of the Israelites was a favor because Pharaoh did not enslave him too.
rows.anchor: لفظ الخبر وفيه تبكيت للمخاطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عبد الرجل and أعبدته both mean to make someone a slave.
rows.anchor: يقال: عبدت الرجل، وأعبدته، اتخذته عبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parse makes أن a nominative apposition to نعمة: Pharaoh enslaved the Israelites but left Moses unenslaved.
rows.anchor: رفع على البدل من نعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively أن is accusative: Pharaoh’s persecution became a benefit because otherwise Moses’ family would have kept him rather than placing him in the river.
rows.anchor: فإنما صارت نعمة بما فعلت من البلاء

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The quoted poem uses أعبدني to mean that the people made the speaker their slave.
rows.anchor: الشاعر في أعبدت اتخذت عبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses answers Pharaoh’s question about the Lord of the Worlds by pointing to the heavens, earth, and everything between them as creations beyond human ability to produce.
rows.anchor: بما خلق مما يعجز المخلوقون عن أن يأتوا بمثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh is confounded and offers no counterargument to Moses’ proof; he turns to the courtiers and asks whether they are listening.
rows.anchor: لم يردد جوابا ينقض به هذا القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses expands the proof to their Lord and their forefathers, then to the Lord of east and west; Pharaoh still cannot refute it and calls the messenger mad.
rows.anchor: فلم يجبه أيضا، فقال: (إن رسولكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses continues the proof with a visible sign witnessed by Pharaoh and his assembly, after Pharaoh threatens to imprison him for taking another god.
rows.anchor: واحتج بما شاهده هو والملأ من حوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ثعبان produced from the staff is a large kind of snake.
rows.anchor: والثعبان الكبير من الحيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the staff’s form a large ثعبان and describing its movement as like a small جان is consistent: its body was large but its motion and agility were light and quick, magnifying the sign.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن خلقها خلق الثعبان واهتزازها وحركتها وخفتها كاهتزاز الجان وخفته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ hand came from his pocket luminous white without disease or leprosy, leaving Pharaoh no answer beyond calling the sign expert sorcery.
rows.anchor: فلم يكن عنده دفع لما شاهده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh labels the sign sorcery, claims Moses intends to expel them from their land, and yields to his followers, who urge delay and a search for magicians.
rows.anchor: ثم استكان وخضع للذين هم من أتباعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أرجه is read with the hāʾ either kasra or ḍamma and with a yāʾ or wāw suffix; it means delay him, while tafsir says detain him and his brother, postponing the debate until an assembly can be gathered.
rows.anchor: وبالياء والواو أرجهي وأرجهو وأخاه

rows.speaker: النحويون
rows.claim: The exception إلا رب العالمين is discontinuous, meaning but the Lord of the Worlds.
rows.anchor: إنه استثناء ليس من الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, because the audience worshipped idols alongside God, Abraham says all they worshipped are his enemies except the Lord of the Worlds, whose worship he does not reject.
rows.anchor: أن جميع من عبدتم عدو لي إلا رب العالمين

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: Tafsir identifies Abraham’s خطيئة with his statement that Sarah was his sister, his claim that the largest idol did it, and his saying that he was sick.
rows.anchor: إن سارة أختي، وقوله بل فعله كبيرهم هذا فاسألوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophets are human and may commit a sin, but they do not commit major sins because they are protected and chosen; each prophet is better than all people of his era.
rows.anchor: وقد يجوز أن يقع عليهم الخطيئة إلا أنهم صلوات الله عليهم لا تكون منهم الكبيرة لأنهم معصومون مختارون على العالمين

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some take the sequence as fronting and delay: Solomon tells the hoopoe to deliver the letter and see the reply, then withdraw; Zajjaj calls this a good reading of the sequence.
rows.anchor: التقديم والتأخير، معناه اذهب بكتابي هذا فألقه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Others read ثم تول عنهم as withdrawing unseen so the hoopoe can watch what answer they give.
rows.anchor: مستترا من حيث لا يرونك، فانظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account omits the hoopoe’s going and delivering the letter because the context makes that action clear.
rows.anchor: لأن في الكلام دليلا عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كتاب كريم means that the letter contains good things.
rows.anchor: ومعنى (كتاب كريم) حسن ما فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophetic letters follow concise, abbreviated expression.
rows.anchor: وكتب الأنبياء صلوات الله عليهم جارية على الإيجاز والاختصار

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A report says the letter was addressed from God’s servant Solomon to Bilqis daughter of Sarahil; people adopted the formula from Solomon.
rows.anchor: إلى بلقيس بنت سراحيل، وإنما كتب الناس من عبد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ألا تعلوا علي means do not exalt yourselves over me, even though you are kings.
rows.anchor: ألا تترفعوا علي وإن كنتم ملوكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will show people His signs in everything He has created and within themselves.
rows.anchor: في جميع ما خلق، وفي أنفسكم

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: Tafsir places Moses’ entry into the city at midday, during the siesta.
rows.anchor: وقت القائلة، وهو انتصاف النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two demonstratives this is from his party and this from his enemy describe absent people as if they were present in the scene.
rows.anchor: وجد فيها رجلين أحدهما من شيعته وأحدهما من عدوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the demonstratives narrate the scene as present: a viewer looking at the two men would say one is from his party and one from his enemy.
rows.anchor: على جهة الحكاية للحضرة، أي فوجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man of Moses’ party was an Israelite, and the man of his enemy’s party was among Pharaoh’s people.
rows.anchor: من بني إسرائيل، والذي من عدوه من أصحاب فرعون

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: Tafsir says Pharaoh was from Istakhr; the slain enemy is variously said to be a Copt or also from Istakhr.
rows.anchor: كان رجلا من أهل اصطخر، ويقال إن الرجل الذي هو من عدوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فاستغاثه means that the Israelite sought Moses’ aid or support.
rows.anchor: أي استنصره، والذي من شيعته من بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فوكزه means Moses killed him by striking with the closed hand; some say he struck him with a stick.
rows.anchor: الوكز أن تضرب بجمع كفك، وقد قيل وكزه بالعصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ words this is from Satan’s work indicate that the killing was accidental and that he had not been commanded to kill or fight.
rows.anchor: أن قتله إياه كان خطأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يستصرخه means he calls for help; الاستصراخ is seeking aid or assistance.
rows.anchor: أي يستغيث به، والاستصراخ الإغاثة والاستنصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Zajjaj’s grammatical reading, the Israelite seeking aid was trying to have Moses strike their shared enemy, but Moses did not do so and called the Israelite plainly misguided.
rows.anchor: فلما أراد المستصرخ أن يبطش موسى بالذي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelite exposed Moses’ earlier killing by revealing it to Pharaoh’s people.
rows.anchor: فأفشى على موسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A saying calls anyone who has killed two people a جبار.
rows.anchor: ويقال إن من قتل اثنين فهو جبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جبار means an arrogant person who will not humble himself before God; unjustly killing one or many people makes a killer a جبار.
rows.anchor: والجبار في اللغة المتعظم الذي لا يتواضع لأمر الله

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: The command is explained as requiring believers to migrate from a place where they cannot worship God and fulfill their obligations, initially applying to those unable to profess their faith openly.
rows.anchor: أمروا بالهجرة من الموضع الذي لا تمكنهم فيه عبادة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rule extends to anyone in a place where sins prevail and one cannot avoid them: they should move somewhere they can worship God properly.
rows.anchor: وكذلك يجب على كل من كان في بلد يعمل فيه بالمعاصي ولا يمكنه بغير ذلك أن يهاجر وينتقل إلى حيث يتهيأ له أن يعبد الله حق عبادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In فإياي فاعبدون, إياي is governed by an implied verb explained by the following one; the latter verb suffices instead of repeating the former.
rows.anchor: المعنى فاعبدوا إياي - فاعبدوني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the phrase is ordered فإياي فاعبدوا, the following verb governs إياي; the initial fāʾ answers an implied condition, as in زيدا فاضرب.
rows.anchor: فإياي منصوب بما بعد الفاء

rows.speaker: النحويون البصريون
rows.claim: The conditional analysis of the initial fāʾ is the position of all Basran grammarians.
rows.anchor: وهذا مذهب جميع النحويين البصريين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading alternates between singular أثر رحمت الله and plural آثار رحمت الله; the plural means traces of rain, which is a mercy from God.
rows.anchor: يعني آثار المطر الذي هو رحمة من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reviving the earth means making it grow; this is analogous to raising the dead, and ذلك refers to God.
rows.anchor: ذلك إشارة إلى الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dead, deaf, and blind are a metaphor for disbelievers who do not act on what they hear or understand what they see; the likeness is also expressed as صم بكم عمي.
rows.anchor: فجعلهم في تركهم العمل بما يسمعون ووعي ما يبصرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s power and creation, beyond what creatures can produce, are evidence of His oneness.
rows.anchor: لأن ما بين من قدرته وصنعته التي لا يقدر على مثلها المخلوقون دليل على وحدانيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first human in the phrase means Adam and his descendants, while Adam himself was created from clay.
rows.anchor: يعني آدم وذريته، فآدم خلق من طين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مهين means weak.
rows.anchor: ومعنى مهين ضعيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سلالة is a small amount drawn from something; the pattern فعالة also appears in فضالة, نخامة, and قوارة.
rows.anchor: الفعالة نحو الفضالة والنخامة والقوارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is read أإنا لفي خلق جديد, أنا لفي خلق جديد, or إنا لفي خلق جديد.
rows.anchor: ويقرأ (أنا لفي خلق جديد)، ويقرأ (إنا لفي خلق جديد)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إذا is accusative; with أإنا, it means will we be resurrected when we have perished, and the following claim that we are in a new creation supplies the understood question.
rows.anchor: على معنى أنبعث إذا ضللنا في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the reading إنا, إذا is governed by ضللنا and gives a conditional meaning; a following fāʾ is unnecessary when إذا is followed by a past-tense verb.
rows.anchor: ويكون بمعنى الشرط والجزاء، ولا يضر ألا يذكر الفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The grammarians agree that إذا cannot be governed by a word occurring after أن.
rows.anchor: لا خلاف بين النحويين في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ضللنا means that they died, became earth and bones, and disappeared so that no trace of their creation remained recognizable.
rows.anchor: إذا متنا فصرنا ترابا وعظاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading with ṣād, صللنا, may mean that bodies rotted and changed, as in the phrase for meat becoming rotten.
rows.anchor: أحدهما أنتنا وتغيرنا، وتغيرت صورنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other explanation of صللنا is that they became like صلة, dry land.
rows.anchor: صرنا من جنس الصلة، وهي الأرض اليابسة
